title: Notion's Token Town — Sarah Sachs, Notion

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk centers on model routing infrastructure, auto model provider swapping, and cost-per-capability platform decisions that other teams build products on. Notion serves both individual productivity and enterprise operations, while the model routing infrastructure is a developer platform-level concern. The discussion covers production model routing and scaling AI products sustainably across vendor relationships. Advanced vendor strategy, cost optimization frameworks, and multi-agent orchestration require significant AI engineering experience. A conference presentation with slides, benchmark comparisons, and a live multi-agent demo. Multiple direct transcript excerpts with specific quantitative figures support each key claim.

summary: Sarah Sachs, who leads AI engineering teams at Notion, frames the talk around building AI products sustainably without falling into token-cost traps. She describes her role negotiating AI contracts as "AI Anna Wintour," emphasizing taste and leverage with model vendors. Notion's AI transformation journey spans four stages: thought partner, assistant, teammate, and system. 88% of people can't get past AI as an assistant due to siloed data and lack of a durable system of record. Cost is the structural barrier: vendors upgrade reasoning models at the same per-token price but burn 3x output tokens, or introduce 40% more expensive models while deprecating predecessors in four months. Companies aren't growing 40% or making 3x revenue to match. Sachs's central argument is that your supplier is your competitor—labs sell first-party products and resell tokens at markup-on-markup with no defensible value. Tying yourself to one provider eliminates exit options; optionality is your leverage regardless of discounts or engineering effort. She advocates winning on product: building data flywheels, understanding customers, knowing when capability vs. price vs. latency matters, and compelling UI/orchestration. Not all traffic belongs on frontier models—triaging an email inbox on Opus rips off both customer and Notion. Notion's auto model handles ~75% of traffic and swaps providers underneath—the "AI Switzerland" approach. The model agnostic playbook includes building for multimodal, thinking about cost per capability per second across entire trajectories (not just single calls), switching fast and often, and exchanging eval expertise with labs instead of committing to large contracts. Open weight models serve moderate tasks and provide negotiation leverage as credible alternatives; the gap between open weights and frontier closes over time. CPUs can handle deterministic tasks like CSV-to-PDF, CLI tool calls, and SQL queries—GPUs aren't necessary for every job. Governance provides visibility, maintainability, and control. The final stretch covers the "lethal trifecta" security concept (private data access + untrusted content exposure + external communication) and a live demo of Notion agents scoping tasks, tagging teammates, opening PRs, and coordinating multi-agent orchestration across coding agents.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

Win on product, not token economics: build data flywheels, orchestration, compelling UI, and understand customer needs better than vendors.
Notion's auto model routes ~75% of traffic and swaps providers underneath—the 'AI Switzerland' approach to model agnosticism.
Route by cost-per-capability-per-second across entire trajectories, not just single calls or token cost.
Open weight models provide a credible alternative for moderate tasks and create downward pricing pressure on the oligopoly; the gap with frontier closes over time.

sections.title: Welcome and introduction
sections.summary: Sarah Sachs introduces herself as leader of AI engineering at Notion, jokes about being called 'AI Anna Wintour' for her role negotiating AI contracts, and frames the talk as sharing Notion's secrets for sustainable AI product building.

sections.title: Notion's AI transformation journey and system of record
sections.summary: Describes four stages of AI transformation—thought partner, assistant, teammate, and system. Notes 88% can't get past AI as assistant due to siloed data. Notion's mission is to be the durable system of record for human-agent collaboration.

sections.title: Cost as structural barrier and monthly pricing traps
sections.summary: Cost is the largest barrier to scaling AI successfully. Vendors trap customers with same-price-but-3x-tokens upgrades or 40% price increases with four-month deprecations. Companies aren't growing proportionally. Fortune 500 can navigate; most others cannot.

sections.title: Your supplier is your competitor
sections.summary: Model vendors selling first-party products are competitors. Buying tokens at markup-on-markup is indefensible. Tying to one provider eliminates exit options. A Dylan analysis showed frontier labs charge very differently for first-party vs. resold products.

sections.title: Win on product, not token economics
sections.summary: Advocates building data flywheels, understanding customers, knowing when capability vs. price vs. latency matters, and compelling UI/orchestration. Stop trying to train the best model; bet on the frontier, not on the lab. Cites Citadel memo on bifurcation of frontier vs. everyday usage.

sections.title: Not all traffic belongs on frontier models
sections.summary: Model provider pricing is an oligopoly racing to the top; price doesn't correlate with capability growth. Second-best models only need to be slightly cheaper. Being outspoken about one lab is a red flag. Model agnosticism is essential because frontier leadership shifts monthly.

sections.title: Model agnostic playbook and auto model
sections.summary: Optionality is your leverage—without the capability to walk, you're stuck. Notion's auto model handles ~75% of traffic and swaps providers underneath (AI Switzerland approach). Playbook: build for multimodal, think about cost per capability per second across entire trajectories not single calls, switch fast and often, exchange eval expertise with labs instead of large financial commits. Parallel web search example shows trajectory-level eval granularity matters more than single-call cost or latency.

sections.title: Open weight models for the moderate middle
sections.summary: Open weight models are strong enough for moderate tasks and RL on top expands their upmarket coverage. They lower cost barriers for customers and provide negotiation leverage as credible alternatives putting downward pressure on oligopoly pricing. Gap with frontier closes over time—if tasks are good enough today, open weights likely cover them in six months. Don't rely only on external benchmarks; develop internal expertise on tool errors and actual latency needs.

sections.title: CPUs over GPUs and governance
sections.summary: Notion launched 'workers' recognizing GPUs aren't necessary for every job. You don't need an LLM to turn a CSV into a PDF, talk to Notion tool calls via CLI, or do deterministic SQL queries—this is where people become token poor. Governance provides visibility, maintainability, and control, offering more to customers when you have model optionality.

sections.title: Security: the lethal trifecta
sections.summary: The lethal trifecta (coined by Simon Wilson): access to private data + exposure to untrusted content (ingestion, MCP, email) + ability to communicate externally. More autonomous systems mean more unsupervised risk. Sandboxes, determinism, and understanding what agents see, do, and persist build valuable product beyond just capability.

sections.title: Live demo: orchestrating Notion agents into a PR
sections.summary: Demo shows Claude agent scoping a task in an active Notion document, asking clarifying questions, tagging in teammates (PM MJ), using Decagon agents for customer voice, iterating with TL, spinning up a PR, and CodeEx reviewing it finding two issues. Notion uses this software factory approach internally for polish and large feedback coordination. Reports over three minutes saved per task and massive ROI gains.

demonstrations: Live demo of Notion agents: Claude scopes a task in an active document, asks clarifying questions, tags in teammates (PM MJ), uses Decagon agents for customer voice data, iterates with TL, spins up a PR, and CodeEx reviews finding two issues.
Benchmark slide comparison of open weight vs. frontier models showing the gap closes over time, originally shown by Philip at BE10.
